---
title: "6 · Applications of Scrambling"
---

So far randomness has been something to *characterize*. Here it becomes a **tool**.
The same Haar second moment that gave the Page formula also underwrites a suite of
practical protocols — and one of the deepest thought experiments in physics.

- **Classical shadows.** Random measurements, followed by an analytic inversion of
  the measurement channel, let you predict many observables of an unknown state
  from surprisingly few copies. The cost is set by a "shadow norm" that scales as
  $3^k$ for $k$-local observables.
- **Randomized benchmarking.** Averaging over random Clifford sequences *twirls*
  complicated gate noise into a single depolarizing parameter, read off from an
  exponential decay — the standard way hardware fidelity is reported.
- **Hayden–Preskill.** If a black hole is a fast scrambler, information thrown in
  re-emerges in its radiation almost immediately — provided you already hold its
  earlier radiation. The decoupling theorem makes this precise, and it is the same
  Page-curve mathematics in disguise.
- **Scrambling and metrology.** Tripartite mutual information becomes a scrambling
  diagnostic, and the fragility of GHZ-state metrology shows the flip side: highly
  non-local information is powerful but delicate.

## Notebooks in this chapter

- [The shadow channel](../notebooks/ch6/solution_ch6_shadow_channel.ipynb) — inverting the measurement channel, the heart of classical shadows.
- [Classical shadows in action](../notebooks/ch6/solution_ch6_numerical_shadows.ipynb) — estimating observables from random measurements.
- [Randomized benchmarking](../notebooks/ch6/solution_ch6_numerical_randomized_benchmarking.ipynb) — extracting gate fidelity from an exponential decay.
- [Tripartite mutual information](../notebooks/ch6/solution_ch6_tripartite_mutual_information.ipynb) — a quantitative diagnostic of scrambling.
- [Fragility of GHZ metrology](../notebooks/ch6/solution_ch6_greenberger_horne_zeilinger_fragility.ipynb) — Heisenberg-scaling sensitivity destroyed by a single lost qubit.
